edge.title: The favour in your luggage
edge.setup: Someone you barely know, a friend of a friend or a new acquaintance at the gate, asks you to carry a small sealed packet, gift or pair of shoes on your trip, just to hand over at the other end. It feels like a favour, and refusing feels rude.
edge.tell: You are being asked to answer for contents you cannot verify, for a person who will not be there if it goes wrong.
move: Say no to anything sealed that you did not pack yourself, however small or friendly the request. A courier exists for exactly this.
If you must carry something for someone you trust, open it, look through it and pack it yourself.
If an item turns up in your bag that you did not pack, tell airport staff before screening, not after.
edge.why: At a checkpoint the bag in your hand is treated as yours. The sender's convenience becomes your problem, and the sender is the one party who knows what is inside. Refusing costs a moment of awkwardness; the downside of agreeing has no ceiling.
edge.variants: Same shape: 'just hold this bag while I step out', delivering a parcel for a tenant, carrying cash or medicine across a border for a stranger.
edge.anchor: A passenger was caught at Bengaluru's KIA airport with ganja hidden in shoes (The Times of India).

lens.name: Opportunity cost
lens.one_line: The true price of anything is the best thing you gave up to get it.
lens.detail: ₹5 lakh in a fixed deposit isn't 'safe' in isolation — its real cost is whatever that money would have done elsewhere, against inflation. Two hours commuting costs whatever those two hours were worth. This is also the honest way to evaluate any 'free' thing: free tends to be paid in time, attention or optionality.
elsewhere: A cheap flat 25 km out, priced in hours of your life per year.
Studying one more degree versus the earnings and experience forgone.
A free app paid for with attention and data.
lens.test: Not 'can I afford this?' but 'what is the best thing I'm giving up to have it?'
lens.today: Karnataka's deputy chief minister told protesting sugarcane farmers the government has only limited funds (The Times of India), and the Metro Phase 4 plan of 215 km puts suburbs first while the core city takes a back seat (Moneycontrol). Each rupee and each kilometre committed to one place is the one not committed to another, so ask what a project displaces, not just what it adds.

moved.what: Safety clearance for the Bannerghatta Road metro line is likely today, and the Supreme Court has allowed BMRCL to go ahead with the Blue Line (Deccan Herald).
moved.so_what: A clearance is not an opening date. Keep your current commute until BMRCL announces the start, then test the new line off-peak before relying on it.

moved.what: Concretising works on Hennur–Bagalur Road have been given a two-month deadline, with an elevated corridor and flyovers also under consideration (The Times of India, Deccan Herald).
moved.so_what: If this road is on your route, plan for slow stretches for up to two months and keep a second route saved.

moved.what: Garbage collection is suffering over a tender standoff with contractors (The Times of India).
moved.so_what: Expect missed pickups. Keep wet waste sealed, and ask your association now what the fallback is if collection slips for several days.

moved.what: A survey found reduced lung function among BMTC drivers, traffic police, pourakarmikas and construction workers (The Hindu).
moved.so_what: The same dust and exhaust is on your daily route. On two-wheelers or in traffic-heavy stretches, a well-fitted N95-grade mask is worth wearing.

moved.what: A group has given the government a November 26 deadline to lift curbs on protest venues in Bengaluru, warning of civil disobedience and a mass stir (The Hindu, The New Indian Express).
moved.so_what: If the deadline passes, expect crowds and diversions in central Bengaluru around Constitution Day. Avoid scheduling anything time-critical there that day.

carry_over.prompt: You are about to buy a used car or two-wheeler; the price is fair and the owner seems decent: what is the one thing missing from the deal?
carry_over.answer: Every claim is from the seller's mouth; none is from a record you fetched yourself.
